mechanisms.statement: Think-SFT imitated teacher traces inside its ChatML template, opened by <think> and closed by a final answer after the thinking block. Where and how it states the answer is learned conditional on that template. On the raw template with the cue it reasons as well but sometimes misplaces the final answer (on the line after 'Answer:'), which v3 misses. Its own template restores the trained ending: more MATH-500 answers counted, unchanged reasoning length and cap behaviour on hard328.

holds_against.why: Raw template without the cue is neither the trained template nor the cue's register, so it loses 16; the native template is the trained one.
The misses are about which line carries the answer, not answer type, so the non-integer share need not rise above the pool's.

mechanisms.statement: Think-SFT copied teacher traces produced under long budgets, and imitation carries no pressure to stop, so its 16,384-token cuts are mid-derivation work, not loops or guesses. More budget turns cut answers right at the problem's difficulty rate (about a quarter on hard328, fewer on 2026 problems). Late finishes are mostly wrong but scattered, so in a vote they seldom beat an existing right answer and add less than to single samples. RL's delta adds stopping, leaving fewer cuts to convert.

holds_against.why: Only the 24 cut answers that switched script before 16k finish right 1 time; the other 69 finish right 22 times, which is the unfinished-work rate the mechanism uses.
The base's late finishes are right 4 of 64 because the base did not imitate long derivations; its cuts are failed solves, the contrast the mechanism expects.

mechanisms.statement: RL-Zero's group-relative reward gives gradient only on prompts where some rollouts succeed and others fail, so early RL moves the policy on problems the base solves sometimes, mostly short and medium ones, and leaves problems the base rarely solves for late training. By step 100 the gain sits on MATH-500's mid-difficulty problems; on hard problems, where the cued base mostly fails or runs to the cap, step 100 plain is no better than the cued base.

holds_against.why: RL learned seen prompts that the base solves only 20.8 % of the time per sample; that rate is not zero, so group-relative gradient exists there, but it needs many steps.
Code 3.1 solves 27 % of the base's 0-of-4 problems, so those problems have a nonzero base rate and enter training late, not never.

mechanisms.statement: Pretraining fixed, for each problem, the base's distribution over final values; the cue picks which register samples it but does not move its modal value. A vote converges to that mode, so its ceiling is the problems whose modal value is right, and samples beyond about eight only resolve ties. The plain prompt samples pretraining's terse solution register, whose accuracy falls faster with difficulty than the cued register's, so plain's share of the cued score shrinks on harder sets.

holds_against.why: Only 43 % of vote failures have agreeing wrong values; the rest are ties, which extra samples resolve, worth a few problems from 4 to 9, then a plateau at the mode.
Self-opened plain draws equal the cue, so the register is chosen at the opening of one pretrained distribution, as the mechanism says, not added by the cue.

mechanisms.statement: The largest singular direction per matrix of RL-Math's change carries the reward's most consistent signal: write the final answer in the boxed form the verifier reads, which also ends some answers. Deciding to stop deliberating on long problems is spread over the next directions. One direction therefore cuts cap hits only partly, and scaling it mostly changes answer form, not stopping: top-1 at 2x gains little over top-1 at 1x, while eight directions together act as the finishing dial.

holds_against.why: One direction already cuts cap hits from 77 to 51; boxing an answer ends it, so a partial stop comes with the format, but the cut from 46 to 5 needs all eight at 2x.
IF's 8 directions finish answers without boxes (158 unboxed); each reward's top direction writes the form its own verifier reads, here IF's, which fits the mechanism.

mechanisms.statement: The RL update is written onto features that pretraining placed in the early and middle layers: the input directions of RL-Math's top-8 change are the ones math text drives most, and most of RL's change in model output comes from layers 0-15. Adding the directions only in the first or middle third therefore gives more of the hard-problem gain than the last third, whose main distinct job, writing the opening cue, is redundant when the cue is prefilled.

holds_against.why: One late tensor (layer 31) writes the cue and gets 397 on the plain prompt; in the layer cells the cue is prefilled, so that late-layer job adds nothing there.
Attention-only 178 against MLP-only 181 splits by module, not by depth; the depth split is untested and the KL split favours layers 0-15.
